\section*{Tight-Binding Hamiltonian}

The real-space matrix elements define

\begin{equation}
  H(\mathbf{k}) = \sum_{\mathbf{R}} e^{i\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{R}}\, H(\mathbf{R}),
\end{equation}

where $\mathbf{k}$ is given in reduced coordinates and $H_{mn}(\mathbf{R}) = \langle \mathbf{0}m | \hat{H} | \mathbf{R}n \rangle$.

The direct-lattice basis vectors used in $\mathbf{R} = R_1\mathbf{a}_1 + R_2\mathbf{a}_2 + R_3\mathbf{a}_3$ are

\begin{align}
  \mathbf{a}_1 &= (2.46, 0, 0) \\
  \mathbf{a}_2 &= (1.23, 2.13042, 0) \\
  \mathbf{a}_3 &= (0, 0, 20)
\end{align}

\medskip

\begin{equation}
  H(\mathbf{k}) \approx \sum_{\text{listed}} t_{mn}(\mathbf{R})\, e^{i\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{R}}\, |m\rangle\langle n| + h.c.,
\end{equation}

\subsection*{Second-quantization form}

The Hamiltonian in second-quantization reads

\begin{equation}
  H = \sum_{\mathbf{k}} \sum_{m,n} H_{mn}(\mathbf{k})\, c^\dagger_{m\mathbf{k}} c_{n\mathbf{k}},
\end{equation}

where $H_{mn}(\mathbf{k}) = \sum_{\mathbf{R}} H_{mn}(\mathbf{R})\, e^{i\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{R}}$.

Expanded term by term (orbital labels: $\text{C:}p_z$, $\text{C:}p_z$):

\begin{align}
H &= \sum_{\mathbf{k}} \Bigl[
      \varepsilon_{\text{C:}p_z}\, c^\dagger_{\text{C:}p_z,\mathbf{k}} c_{\text{C:}p_z,\mathbf{k}}
    +   \varepsilon_{\text{C:}p_z}\, c^\dagger_{\text{C:}p_z,\mathbf{k}} c_{\text{C:}p_z,\mathbf{k}} \\
  &\quad +   f_{\text{C:}p_z \to \text{C:}p_z}(\mathbf{k})\, c^\dagger_{\text{C:}p_z,\mathbf{k}} c_{\text{C:}p_z,\mathbf{k}}
    +   f_{\text{C:}p_z \to \text{C:}p_z}^*(\mathbf{k})\, c^\dagger_{\text{C:}p_z,\mathbf{k}} c_{\text{C:}p_z,\mathbf{k}}
  \Bigr],
\end{align}

where the on-site energies are

\begin{align}
  \varepsilon_{\text{C:}p_z} &= \operatorname{Re}[H_{\text{C:}p_z,\text{C:}p_z}(\mathbf{0})] = 0\text{ eV} \\
  \varepsilon_{\text{C:}p_z} &= \operatorname{Re}[H_{\text{C:}p_z,\text{C:}p_z}(\mathbf{0})] = 0\text{ eV}
\end{align}

The structure functions are defined as

\begin{align}
  f_{\text{C:}p_z \to \text{C:}p_z}(\mathbf{k}) &= -2.7\,e^{i\mathbf{k}\cdot(-\mathbf{a}_1)}
    - 2.7\,e^{i\mathbf{k}\cdot(-\mathbf{a}_2)}
    - 2.7\, \\
\end{align}
